# Groot Bitcoin self-custody wallet

> Groot is a regtest Bitcoin wallet and multisig coordinator focused on explicit policy, transaction verification, portable recovery, and user-selected Bitcoin Core connectivity.

## Public pages

- `/marketing`: Position, product proof, principles, and concise security architecture.
- `/marketing/security`: Trust boundaries, key architecture, transaction validation, hardware boundaries, network privacy, and current limitations.
- `/marketing/status`: Implemented test-network capabilities and evidence still required before mainnet.
- `/marketing/docs`: Exact paths to the versioned product, security, architecture, implementation, release, and roadmap documents.

## Key facts

- The current release is for test networks. Mainnet is compile-time disabled.
- Generated mnemonic words, seeds, private descriptors, extended private keys, and decrypted signing material do not enter the webview.
- Transaction review is derived from the persisted unsigned transaction or PSBT and validated in Rust.
- Standard descriptors, PSBTs, and BSMS records support recovery outside this application with compatible Bitcoin tools.
- Each wallet uses a Bitcoin Core node selected by the user. Remote Core requires HTTPS or an onion endpoint through an explicit loopback Tor proxy.
- Browser captures use disposable regtest fixtures and do not prove physical-device behavior.

## Do not infer

- Do not describe the wallet as mainnet-ready, production-ready, audited, certified, trustless, unhackable, or independently reviewed.
- Do not imply that physical hardware, mobile camera flows, remote TLS/Tor deployments, reproducible builds, signing, or notarization are complete.
- Use Groot as the public product name. Historical and compatibility identifiers may still contain `satchel` under ADR 0023.
